awards.display_name: THE TRANSITING EXOPLANET SURVEY SATELLITE (TESS)  SET TO LAUNCH IN MARCH  WILL PERFORM A TWO-YEAR ALL-SKY SURVEY WITH THE PRIMARY GOAL OF DETECTING SMALL NEPTUNE AND EARTH-LIKE ANALOGUES AROUND BRIGHT  NEARBY STARS. THE RESULTING SET OF EXTRASOLAR PLANETS WILL SERVE AS TARGETS FOR NASAS JAMES WEBB SPACE TELESCOPE (JWST) TO OBSERVE AND CHARACTERIZE THEIR ATMOSPHERES. THIS PROPOSAL WILL CREATE A LARGE  GROUND-BASED  HIGH-PRECISION SPECTROSCOPIC FOLLOW-UP PROGRAM TO ROBUSTLY VET TESS OBJECTS OF INTEREST (TOIS). TOIS ARE SYSTEMS WHICH SHOW A TRANSIT AND MAY BE GENUINE EXOPLANETS. WHILE THE TESS TEAM AND THE ASTROPHYSICAL COMMUNITY HAVE DEVELOPED SOME IDEAS FOR VETTING  THIS PROPOSAL GREATLY COMPLEMENTS THE EXISTING TOOLS BY BRINGING IN NEW OBSERVATIONAL INSTRUMENTS ADEPT FOR CLASSIFYING AND DYNAMICALLY CHARACTERIZING TOIS. THIS PROPOSAL WILL USE THE APACHE POINT OBSERVATORY GALAXY EVOLUTION EXPERIMENT (APOGEE) SPECTROGRAPH ON THE SLOAN FOUNDATION 2.5-METER TELESCOPE  THE HABITABLE ZONE PLANET FINDER (HPF) ON THE HOBBY-EBERLY TELESCOPE  AND THE NASA/NSF SPONSORED NNEXPLORE EXOPLANET INVESTIGATIONS WITH DOPPLER SPECTROSCOPY (NEID) SPECTROGRAPH ON THE WIYN TELESCOPE. APOGEE IS CAPABLE OF OBSERVING 300 STARS SIMULTANEOUSLY AT A PRECISION NECESSARY TO CONFIRM IF A TOI IS AN EXOPLANET OR AN ASTROPHYSICAL FALSE POSITIVE. IT HAS CURRENTLY OBSERVED OVER 70 000 TESS STARS  MOST WITH MULTIPLE OBSERVATIONS. HPF AND NEID CAN ONLY OBSERVE ONE TARGET BUT AT THE PRECISION NECESSARY TO DERIVE PRECISE EXOPLANETS MASSES. APOGEE DATA WILL CULL A LARGE NUMBER OF TOIS TO DEFINE A SUBSET OF TESS STARS HOSTING TRUE PLANETS IN NEED OF FURTHER CHARACTERIZATION BY HPF AND NEID. THE END PRODUCT IS A SUBSET OF TOIS WITH PRECISE DYNAMICAL MASSES AND RADII THAT CAN BE OBSERVED BY JWST. THIS PROPOSAL IS DIRECTLY ALIGNED WITH THE THEME OF EXOPLANET EXPLORATION WITHIN THE SOLICITATION AND THE BROADER GOALS OF NASA TO DISCOVER AND STUDY PLANETS AROUND OTHER STARS AND EXPLORE WHETHER THEY COULD HARBOR LIFE. THERE IS A DIRECT APPLICATION TO THE SUCCESS OF TESS AND JWST  TWO CURRENT NASA MISSIONS  BY PROVIDING A SET OF VERIFIED EXOPLANETS WITH PRECISE MASSES AND RADII. FUTURE PROGRAMS  SUCH AS THE PROPOSED MISSIONS CONTRIBUTION TO THE ATMOSPHERIC REMOTE-SENSING EXOPLANET LARGE-SURVEY SPECTROSCOPY OF EXOPLANETS (CASE) OR FAST INFRARED EXOPLANET SPECTROSCOPY SURVEY EXPLORER (FINESSE)  WHICH ARE DESIGNED TO EXPLORE THE ATMOSPHERE OF CONFIRMED EXOPLANETS  WILL ALSO BENEFIT FROM THE RESULTS FROM THIS PROPOSAL BY CONSERVING LIMITED OBSERVATION TIME FOR THE HIGHEST PRIORITY PLANETS
